God of War Ragnarök is an absolute masterpiece and one of the best story-driven games I’ve ever played. The journey of Kratos and Atreus feels deeply emotional, powerful, and unforgettable from start to finish.

The combat is smooth, brutal, and incredibly satisfying, with every weapon feeling impactful. The world design is stunning, the boss fights are epic, and the soundtrack perfectly captures the scale of the adventure.

What truly makes this game special is its storytelling. It balances intense action with heartfelt moments, character growth, and a beautifully written narrative inspired by Norse mythology.

A must-play for anyone who loves cinematic, story-rich games.

What a game. Gorgeous art direction, an intense and versatile combat system, and a genuinely compelling story about personal growth and father-son bonding. Fantastic all around.

Note however that the game assumes you're an absolute idiot. NPCs will shout out puzzle solutions before you can even try to solve them - and that’s with the "Reduced Puzzle Hints" setting turned on!

That aside, it's an amazing experience and well worth playing.

God of War Ragnarök is not a game that will please all fans of the series. In fact, it alienates many fans, something that has been happening for some time within the PlayStation family. Those who gave this game a chance and enjoyed it found a truly good adventure that takes Kratos down a different path than expected, but a path no less valid than the one fans would have hoped for.

We are but a sum of our choices!

So I choose this game over any multiplayer!! :)

We are not our failures. We are not who we were. We must be better. 

A true successor to GoW 2018, God of War Ragnarök delivers an even greater cast of characters, lores and deeper storytelling that our favourite Father & Son duo faces while fighting prophecy and fate and growing their love, understanding and trust for one another.
The story have its fair share of serious notes like grief, loss, sorrow, anger as well as things like love, compassion, camaraderie and great amount of comic relief as well. I sometimes laughed out lough with the conversations of Mimir, Kratos, Arteus and other and the funny banters they share.
The game also nicely takes the norse mythology and gives a appropriate spin to it, keeping the sources true but the methods different from what we know about. A really smart way of storytelling and integrating our main characters into the events of Ragnarök.

All in all, God of War Ragnarök made me enjoy a good 60-70 hours of cinematic masterpiece, moments of heart-warming and sad emotions, laughter, joy and an amazing experience and make me fall in love with story-based game like this all over again. Highly recommended.

Ragnarok is more of everything that was great in the 2018 release, combined with the epic scale of the original trilogy.
The continuing story is outstanding, with thoroughly developed characters along with so much lore to chew on as well as really heartfelt moments. Looks incredible and features once again brilliant voice acting (and mocap). Exceptionally well crafted environments and realms make exploration so fun, especially with the way they evolve throughout the story.
Combat is as satisfying, brutal and rewarding as ever with some truly breath-taking boss fights.
An undeniably superlative experience.

This game is actually one of the best masterpieces in story telling and combat mechanics. It is not even close to the difficulty of a souls-like game, but each boss has a purpose, and a story behind it. You're not fighting empty machines with a selected amount of patterns that are waiting for you to beat them. Instead, you're fighting against gods, literal oppressors, that have a deep desire for control. Some themes made me reflect on the real world, like the downsides of industrialization. 

Overall, great game, great mechanics, great fictional story. If you played GOW 2018, everything feels smoother and you feel more in control of Kratos than ever.

The maps take a little getting used to, after that I think the dialog and boss battles easily carry the game and make this a worthy successor to the original. Good game and I advise people to give it a go.

I was worried that Ragnarok would somehow not live up to the first game but was quickly proven wrong. Nearly everything that I enjoyed about GOW 2018 returned just as good if not better - the writing, the performance, Bear McCreary's score, the combat. It's a massive followup (for better or worse) from the scale and depth of the story, the characters, the variety of elements that was packed into every realm.

Towards the final act I was looking forward to it ending, so I'd say GOW 2018 has the upper hand in being the leaner game. But there is so much to take away from Ragnarok's narrative thematically and emotionally, and to follow the relationships between the characters was a roller coaster. I'd say Ragnarok had a lot more heartwarming moments, but the heartbreaking ones can be severe.

It's an amazing sequel and an incredible game, and I hope someday Santa Monica Studios will grace us with another entry.

This is great. If you liked the previous game you'll like this one. 

Saw many reviews saying this is not as good as the previous game - I don't agree and think that many reviewers probably rushed through the main story to get reviews out early as possible. 
There's loads of content here, everything you would have had from the first game and more. The main story is great and really develops the relationship between Kratos and Atreus (along with many others - returning and new). Side quests are also equally good - some are short sure, many are as good as anything the main quest delivers.
The lore and history is there and all the way throughout brilliantly delivered with excellent voice actors. If you liked Mimirs stories while getting around there's plenty of those. 
The combat is exactly what you can expect from a series that is known for it. Combat is a real pleasure in the game and challenging at high levels without being irritating or unfair.

The game is gorgeous to look at and runs beautifully for me on whats now a mid range system. 

Well worth a buy in my opinion and reviews have been unfair from some, misguided in others. I have nearly 50 hours in the game now, I suspect I'm nearing the end of the main story, while not rushing it or being a completionist. I feel theres anywhere between 50 and 80 hours here depending on your levels of completionist.

tldr.text: Very Positive (90%): players love the story and characters, and 58% of reviews praise them.
The main complaint is bugs and crashes.

details.text: Players who review early are roughly split, while veterans with the most hours are 95% positive.
Bugs and crashes fell from 10% of all reviews to 2% of recent ones, so buyers now see far fewer complaints about them.
